propositions: The test derives a renamed project key by replacing the final character with 'Z', causing a collision when the original key already ends in 'Z' (~1 in 26 probability).
When harness draws a project key ending in 'Z' (e.g., RBJDRDZ), the derivation RBJDRD + Z produces an identical key, violating the setup assertion new_project_key != jira_dc_project.
The collision is not a product defect but a flawed key-derivation algorithm in the test itself, independent of any recent changes.
The setup assertion caught the collision and prevented a silent rename-to-self, which was the intended safety mechanism.
A deterministic unit test parametrizing all 26 possible final letters confirms the fixed derivation cannot produce collisions for any valid harness-generated key.
